items.title: Al Vollmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 8, 2017
items.q: in a rash moment I said to Clyde, “We ought to form a band.” And he said, “Well okay, if you’ll take care of most of the business part, you know, I’ll certainly go along.” So that’s how the Harlem Blues and Jazz Band formed.

ctx.x: Well how it started was that the orthodontic practice I started in ’61 became successful and we bought a big house down on the Long Island Sound, 18-room Tudor house, and there were only three of us in it — my wife, my daughter and myself. And we could have a hundred people. And by that time I’d gotten to know quite a few jazz musicians and we decided to have some parties. And they were unusual parties because everybody brought a dish of some kind and we had probably a preponderance of black musicians, although…

You know? It was a dream come true. And so at one point I got to know Clyde Bernhardt and so on March 5th or March 3rd, 1973, at one of the parties, in a rash moment I said to Clyde, “We ought to form a band.” And he said, “Well okay, if you’ll take care of most of the business part, you know, I’ll certainly go along.” So that’s how the Harlem Blues and Jazz Band formed. From these parties. And this was 1973 and we made our first trip to Scandinavia in ’76. Now I was in my 40s and the guys were all in their 60s.
How did you balance that with your work life?
